quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): consolidated net sales JPY 1,307,560 million (+8.8% year on year), operating income JPY 63,856 million (+35.8%), ordinary income JPY 75.9 billion (+56.4%), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 72.5 billion (+117.4%), helped by extraordinary gains including a JPY 19.3 billion gain on sale of investment securities and a JPY 19.4 billion gain from a retirement benefit plan revision. Sales rose on data-center products such as optical fiber cable, automotive parts such as wire harnesses, and the surge in copper prices; profit rose on higher sales, productivity improvements and selling-price optimization. Overseas sales were JPY 662.0 billion (+3.8%), 50.6% of net sales. By segment: Infrastructure net sales JPY 370,856 million (+20.0%) and operating income JPY 21,439 million (+276.1%) - in Information & Communication Solutions (external sales JPY 227,597 million vs JPY 164,269 million a year earlier), data-center demand drove development and sales of high-value-added products such as rollable ribbon cable, MT ferrules and DFB laser diode chips, with capacity investment, a renewed global operating structure for the optical fiber and cable business and a stronger optical fiber cable sales set-up in North America; Energy Infrastructure sales and profit were flat year on year. Electrical & Electronics net sales JPY 765,067 million (+3.9%), operating income JPY 33,887 million (+3.9%). Functional Products net sales JPY 161,089 million (+9.6%), operating income JPY 15,379 million (+8.9%), on thermal management / cooling products, semiconductor manufacturing tape (a new plant began operating during the year) and electrolytic copper foil for high-frequency boards, driven by data-center investment. Services & Development operating loss JPY 6,703 million. No external customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated net sales, so no major customer is disclosed.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 1,307,560 million (+8.8%); operating income JPY 63,856 million (+35.8%); Infrastructure sales JPY 370,856 million (+20.0%), OP JPY 21,439 million (+276.1%); Information & Communication Solutions external sales JPY 227,597 million (vs JPY 164,269 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Targets and strategy (annual securities report; the company numbers fiscal years by their starting year, so its fiscal 2025 is the year ended March 2026): the company's fiscal 2030 financial targets are operating income of JPY 250.0 billion, ROE of 20% and ROIC of 15%. It plans total investment of JPY 650.0 billion over the five years to fiscal 2030 (of which JPY 500.0 billion in focus areas), with five-year free cash flow of JPY 240.0 billion. Toward 2030 it will concentrate management resources on the data-center field, where demand keeps expanding, accelerating investment in data-center-related businesses (defined as Lightera, Thermal, FITEL, AT (semiconductor manufacturing tape), MD (memory disk), copper foil and opto-electronic integration devices). Management states that the global data-center market is expected to grow strongly on the rapid spread of AI, with capacity and density accelerating, that it will keep expanding sales of optical products for data centers while shifting to higher-value-added products and solutions, and that it expects large HVDC and renewable grid investment as data-processing growth raises power demand. All financial targets of the 2025 mid-term plan for fiscal 2025 (year ended March 2026) were achieved: ROIC (after tax) 12.2% vs 6% or more, ROE 19.1% vs 11% or more, consolidated net sales JPY 1.3 trillion vs JPY 1.1 trillion or more, consolidated operating income JPY 63.9 billion vs JPY 58.0 billion or more.
quarterly_data.figure: Fiscal 2030 targets: operating income JPY 250.0 billion; ROE 20%; ROIC 15%; five-year investment JPY 650.0 billion (JPY 500.0 billion focus areas)

quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (annual securities report): to capture data-center demand the company is expanding supply capacity mainly for heat sinks, DFB laser chips and modules, ultra-high-fiber-count rollable ribbon (RR) cable solutions and copper foil for high-frequency boards; during the 2025 mid-term plan it decided on expansion investments in water-cooled module plants for thermal products (Philippines, Hiratsuka) and a new DFB laser chip plant for FITEL (FFT Thailand), and will invest further in stages after confirming returns. It will widen direct contact with major customers including large cloud providers (hyperscalers), proposing its technology from the product-specification stage, and work ahead of demand on CPO (co-packaged optics) and next-generation thermal products. Capex in the year ended March 2026 was JPY 56,662 million (+46.8%): Infrastructure JPY 25,432 million (mainly capacity for optical semiconductor devices and optical fiber, and a power cable manufacturing base), Electrical & Electronics JPY 14,332 million, Functional Products JPY 9,743 million (mainly a new water-cooled module plant for data centers), Services & Development JPY 4,176 million. The capex plan for the following year is JPY 150,000 million: Optical Solutions JPY 25,000 million (optical fiber capacity), Information Components JPY 70,500 million (new water-cooled module plant; optical semiconductor device capacity), Energy Infrastructure JPY 23,600 million (power cable manufacturing base), Automotive Systems JPY 12,200 million, Metal Solutions JPY 5,800 million, Services & Development JPY 12,900 million. It is also building an HVDC cable plant (Futtsu, Chiba), scheduled to start operating in 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 56,662 million (+46.8%); next-year plan JPY 150,000 million incl. Information Components JPY 70,500 million and Optical Solutions JPY 25,000 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optical R&D and CPO (annual securities report): group R&D spending was JPY 28,423 million (+11.7%), of which Infrastructure JPY 15,808 million. The company is developing opto-electronic integration and co-packaged optics (CPO) technology for low power and high-density mounting in data centers; in fiscal 2025 it developed a small optical connector for CPO (Snap-Beam Connector) that connects photonic integrated circuits (PIC) to optical fiber, confirmed low-loss connection with a 40-channel connector and a PIC surface-coupled connector, showed it at OFC2026 and is running customer evaluations toward commercialization. It says it was the first in the world to succeed in a demonstration of a 1,000 km-class space-division-multiplexed optical network using a spatial cross-connect and multicore fiber amplifiers, and reached what it calls world-leading low loss and low crosstalk for a 2-core submarine fiber at pre-mass-production scale. On June 9, 2026 it decided to absorb its wholly owned subsidiary Furukawa FITEL Optical Components (FFOC) effective April 1, 2027, so that data-center optical device and component products, where platforms change very fast, are run in one structure from element technology to customer promotion.
quarterly_data.figure: Group R&D JPY 28,423 million (+11.7%); Infrastructure R&D JPY 15,808 million; 40-channel CPO connector

quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Thermal and copper foil for data centers (annual securities report): the company is developing water cooling in addition to air cooling for data-center CPUs and GPUs; it expanded the water-cooled module plant at its main site FURUKAWA ELECTRIC THERMAL MANAGEMENT SOLUTIONS & PRODUCTS LAGUNA (Philippines) and added equipment at its Hiratsuka plant, preparing for mass production starting September 2026. With printed circuit boards for routers, switches, antennas and generative-AI / data-center servers moving to higher frequencies, it began mass production of the next-generation high-frequency PCB copper foil F0X-WS and is developing further products. Functional Products R&D was JPY 3,006 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Water-cooled module mass production from September 2026; Functional Products R&D JPY 3,006 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Furukawa Electric annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New businesses (annual securities report): in superconductors the company supplies high-temperature superconducting (HTS) wire, centred on SuperPower Inc. (US), and expects HTS wire demand to grow as fusion power is verified; it has built a partnership with UK fusion developer Tokamak Energy through an investment of about GBP 10 million and HTS wire supply, and signed a memorandum toward a jointly operated base in Japan. With Nichia it co-developed a 5 kW blue laser oscillator, which it calls world-highest-level brightness from an optical fiber. Its 24 GHz automotive peripheral-monitoring radar reached 10 million cumulative units shipped. A demonstration plant for green LP gas in Shikaoi, Hokkaido is scheduled to start operating during the company's fiscal 2026 (the year after the one this report covers). Electrical & Electronics R&D was JPY 4,139 million and Services & Development R&D JPY 5,469 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Tokamak Energy investment about GBP 10 million; 5 kW blue laser; 24 GHz radar 10 million cumulative units
